rationale: This is a mechanical recombination of two archived signals (BroadIntangibleCapitalCleanAccruals' bet leg with ChronicCleanAccrualIntangibleCapital's gate) whose own stated hypothesis predicts dilution, so it is an ablation of the current best signal rather than a new economic bet.

A single-operator swap (ZSCORE→IND_ZSCORE) on the archived best signal is a cosmetic variant, and the archive already contains both industry-demeaned and raw versions of adjacent constructs from which the sector-tilt question could largely be answered.

Besides being a pure denominator ablation of the archived winner, scaling by ceq is internally hazardous — negative or near-zero book equity flips the sign of the intangible-capital measure for exactly the distressed, heavily-expensing firms the hypothesis targets, and 1% winsorization does not repair a sign inversion.

The reasoning is internally honest (correctly noting the outer RANK is monotone and thus leaves decile alphas identical, isolating the FMB-attenuation question), and the one substantive change — 3-year accrual smoothing carried to the negative-side leader — is a defensible, economically motivated port, though the incremental content over WithinIndustryIntangibleGatedAccruals is modest.

This is the first output-based (return-on-intangible-capital) leg in the family and the R&D-capitalized denominator is a coherent comparability fix, but be aware the bet leg is close to Novy-Marx gross profitability with a Peters–Taylor style denominator, so any alpha must be shown to exceed what plain GP/AT plus an accrual gate already delivers.

The hard gate is miscalibrated because ib − oancf is negative for the large majority of firms (depreciation alone drives it below zero), so "conservative accruers" is not a selective subsample, and zeroing the remainder creates a huge mass of tied observations that will make the middle decile portfolios arbitrary and the FMB slope hard to interpret.
